canonicalExplanation.summary: Your React single-page app project brings the whole course together: **semantic components**, clear **state ownership**, explicit **data states**, **routes** that survive refresh, **error boundaries**, **tests**, a verified **production build**, and a **hosting fallback**. "All screens look right" is not the finish line. It's done when the key learner journeys work by **keyboard**, on a **phone-width screen**, on a **refreshed deep link**, with **slow and failing requests**, and when automated tests prove it. A short README explains how to run, test and deploy it.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
Your portfolio app looks great in the demo. Then a reviewer refreshes `/projects/quiz-app` and gets a 404, tabs through the nav and loses focus, turns on slow 3G and sees a blank page, and finds the build was never run. A portfolio app supports direct route refresh, loading and error recovery, keyboard navigation, tests, and a verified production bundle. In this lesson you'll deliver and explain a reproducible React SPA whose key user journeys pass automated and manual keyboard tests.


sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Accessibility, errors and performance** module, the **Routing and application context** module, **Routing and integration tests**, **Error boundaries and recovery**, and **Measure before optimization**.

sections.heading: The model: a journey passes only when every layer does
sections.body:
| Layer | Evidence for "done" |
|---|---|
| semantics. | native elements, names; keyboard audit passes. |
| state ownership. | each value has one owner; no duplicated state. |
| data states. | loading, empty, error with retry, success for each fetch. |
| routes. | direct URL, links, Back, not-found; titles and focus move. |
| errors. | route boundaries with safe fallback and retry. |
| tests. | component, async and route integration tests pass in CI. |
| build. | `npm ci && npm run build && npm run preview` works from a clean clone. |
| hosting. | fallback serves index.html; refreshing a deep link works. |
| performance. | one measured check; changes justified or none needed. |

```text
README excerpt.
Run: npm ci, then npm run dev.
Test: npm test (component, async, route suites).
Build: npm run build, then npm run preview.
Deploy: host rewrites /* to /index.html.
Key journeys: browse projects, open a project, contact form.
```

```reveal
{"prompt": "Why list \"key journeys\" in the README?", "answer": "It tells reviewers what to try, and it tells you which journeys need integration tests and a keyboard check."}
```

sections.heading: Manual checks still matter

includes: Integrate components, state, data states, routes, errors, tests and build into one SPA.
Verify key journeys by keyboard, narrow screen, slow network and deep-link refresh, and document them.

outcomes: Deliver and explain a reproducible React SPA whose key user journeys pass automated and manual keyboard tests.

examples.title: A portfolio app that holds up
examples.situation: A portfolio app supports direct route refresh, loading and error recovery, keyboard navigation, tests, and a verified production bundle.
walkthrough: **Direct route refresh:** the host rewrites app paths to index.html, and a route test starts at /projects/quiz-app.
**Loading and error recovery:** each project fetch shows loading, an error with Try again, and success; a route boundary catches render errors.
**Keyboard, tests and bundle:** a keyboard pass will reach every link, CI runs the test suites, and `npm run build && npm run preview` is checked before deploy.
examples.result: Reviewers can refresh any page, use it without a mouse, survive a failing network, and reproduce it from the README.

examples.title: The contact form that sent twice
examples.situation: In the finished app, the contact form sends two emails when the Send button is double-clicked on a slow connection.
walkthrough: The mutation had no pending state.
Add status pending with a disabled button and a ref guard, and show a success or error message.
Add an async test that double-clicks with a slow fake and asserts one call.
examples.result: One message is sent per submission, and the test keeps it that way.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Finishing all visible screens is sufficient evidence that an SPA is complete.
misconceptions.correction: Screens show the happy path. Completion means key journeys work through refreshes, keyboard use, narrow screens, slow and failing requests and production builds, with tests and a README as evidence.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "A portfolio app that holds up", what did the reviewer find?

analogy.example: Shipping an SPA is like **a building inspection**. The rooms may look finished, but the inspector checks every entrance (deep links), the stairs and ramps (keyboard access), the fire exits (error recovery), the wiring under load (slow network), and the paperwork (README and tests).
limitations: Inspectors visit once; your tests inspect on every change.
A beautiful room with a locked door (404 on refresh) still fails.

steps.explanation: Direct route refresh works and shows a loading state.
Loading and error recovery let the learner try again.
Keyboard navigation reaches everything, backed by tests and a verified production bundle.

trace.textAlternative: Walking one key journey. Step 1, Refresh: server is index.html; status is loading. Direct route refresh works and shows a loading state. Step 2, Recover: first request is failed; after retry is project shown. Loading and error recovery let the learner try again. Step 3, Keyboard: focus order is nav, h1, content, contact link. Keyboard navigation reaches everything, backed by tests and a verified production bundle.

nearTransfer.prompt: Write the "done" checklist for one journey in your SPA (for example, opening a project), with one automated test and one manual check per layer.

farTransfer.prompt: Finish your SPA: implement the key journeys, add component, async and route tests, run a keyboard and 360px audit, throttle the network, verify the production build and hosting fallback, and write a README a reviewer can follow.
expectedEvidence: All journeys pass automated and manual checks.

remediation.explanation: For each key journey, walk the table: **semantics, state, data states, routes, errors, tests, build, hosting, performance.** Any row without evidence isn't done yet.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The contact form that sent twice".

recap.summary: To deliver and explain a reproducible React SPA, integrate semantic components, single-owner state, explicit data states, refresh-safe routes with titles and focus, error boundaries, and component, async and route tests, then verify key journeys by keyboard, narrow screen, slow network and deep-link refresh, and document how to run, test and deploy it.
